parsed.explanation: Combined regime is dominated by federal visitor-facing exposures the protective division law does not cancel: passport/visa discrepancy can lead to refusal and possible lifetime fraud ineligibility, federal and many subnational facility bans with a documented trespass arrest, and immigration-custody reports of forced labour, beatings and sexual abuse plus hormone-removal in corrections. Litigation has blocked some orders and the division shields travelling families seeking youth care and historically used identity-based prison housing, but the latter is only documented to Jan 2021, division facility/document status is undocumented, and the 198 raw incident count has no denominator. This is tier-1/2 exposure with partial, contested recourse, above organised street targeting but below a single unremedied facility rule.

entry_documents.exposure: Federal binary sex-marker policy stopped X passports, Supreme Court allowed it; entry cable directs refusal where documents cast reasonable doubt on sex and consideration of permanent fraud ineligibility for wilful misrepresentation. Passports reportedly confiscated/blocked.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports valid until expiry; fraud finding requires four elements, is never automatic, limited waivers exist; civil-liberties suit and legal-aid guidance ongoing.
entry_documents.interaction: Division sanctuary/care law does not override federal entry screening; a discrepancy at the border can move visitor into refusal or detention despite division protections.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Immigration custody: trans men reportedly forced labour, beatings, solitary and severe sexual abuse. National corrections bureau adopted hair-cutting, hormone removal and psychiatric substitution model; stopped reporting trans prisoner numbers.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Division coded Jan 2021 as allowing identity-based housing in general population and funded inmate surgery in 2015; no post-2021 confirmation documented.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Visa/document discrepancy can lead to immigration detention, where documented custody abuse applies; division prison posture does not govern federal custody.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Executive order bars trans people from government-funded single-sex facilities congruent with identity. 21 subnational units ban such use in government buildings/schools; 4 make it criminal in circumstances, with a documented handcuffed trespass arrest and 24h men's-ward hold.
federal_state_facilities.protection: 29 units plus capital district have no mapped ban, but dossier does not document which category this division is in; some orders enjoined.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Federal facilities and any applicable subnational ban apply regardless of division youth-care shield; no operative pre-emption documented.

care_services.exposure: Federal orders characterise youth gender-affirming care as mutilation, proposed rules would bar public-insurance reimbursement under 18, and hospitals were subpoenaed for minor records; several orders blocked/enjoined, present effect uncertain.
care_services.protection: Division Sept 2022 sanctuary law: first to allow youth from outside to obtain hormones/blockers there and shields families from child-abuse investigation or criminal prosecution for seeking care.
care_services.interaction: State shield protects against division-level investigation/prosecution for travelling families, but does not cancel federal funding, entry, school-investigation or hospital-record exposure.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Federal framing includes counterterrorism priority against groups described as radically pro-transgender and use of radical gender ideology in extremism guidance; 2025 poll 66% supported assigned-sex documents.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity; 2020 Supreme Court employment ruling; courts have enjoined several orders and passport suit remains litigated.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official threat framing raises outing and enforcement risk, while functioning courts provide partial but unresolved recourse and have also allowed passport restriction to take effect.

minors_guardians.exposure: Federal order directs investigation of schools promoting gender ideology and criminal prosecution of teachers facilitating social transition; 27 units ban youth care nationally contextually.
minors_guardians.protection: Division shield expressly covers families travelling there for care, protecting them from division child-abuse investigations and criminal prosecution.
minors_guardians.interaction: For a travelling minor, division shield is operative for care, but federal school, funding and record demands create a conflicting federal layer with no documented pre-emption.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Division recorded 198 of 1,000+ nationwide anti-LGBTQ incidents in 2025 by raw count with no population denominator, and largest-city anti-LGBTQ hate-crime reports rose dramatically; neither establishes a trans-specific visitor rate.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime coverage exists; 22 units plus capital district outlaw gender-identity/expression discrimination, but this division's statute coverage is deliberately not documented.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Raw-count hostility cannot be converted to per-capita visitor risk; police response to trans-specific violence in division is not documented.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Passport restriction upheld Nov 2025; facility, entry and custody remedies are litigated and inconsistent; post-2021 prison housing, division bathroom/document rules and detention outcomes remain unresolved.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Multiple suits, enjoined orders, legal-aid FAQ and division care shield show some recourse operating; not shown to change entry, federal-facility or federal-custody rules.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Partial court relief mitigates some federal orders but efficient enforcement of the passport and facility rules that remain in effect is itself exposure.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar tier-1 unremedied institutional exposure plus accepting private settings and no effective override. This case adds federal entry fraud risk and reported federal custody sexual abuse/forced labour, but adds a real youth-care shield and court injunctions, so roughly similar, slightly mitigated.

Lower than 0.45-A: that case is a single birth-sex bathroom rule with polite public and one prosecuted assault, no custody abuse or entry fraud risk. Here federal facilities, entry refusal/ineligibility and severe custody reports are additional documented exposures.

Higher than 0.25-A: no documented routine police raids/extortion sweeps in this division, presentation itself is not a national crime, courts block some orders, and a division care shield operates. Federal custody/entry coercion keeps it well below reduced-risk anchors.

parsed.synthesis: Rate the final interaction, not the most protective component: a trans visitor may enter under federal document scrutiny, use facilities under federal/many-state birth-sex rules, and if detained face documented federal custody abuse, while the division shield mainly protects travelling families seeking youth care from division prosecution and may offer identity-based prison housing of uncertain currency. Courts provide partial relief but also allowed the passport rule. No documented pre-emption cancels federal exposure, and raw incident counts do not prove a per-capita violence rate. Hence elevated-to-high risk, anchored near 0.35.
